sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mythology is the body of tales that carries a culture's faith and customs. Some peoples set these tales down in writing. Their gods then take a settled order, a pantheon. The Celts did not write their myths down. They recited them. So no one book stands as the Celtic scripture. Sculpture and inscriptions came late, from the Roman age, and the Romans read Celtic gods as their own. This has blurred the line of what the Celts first believed. Many tales were written by Christian monks. Their copies may carry touch of the later faith. So the study of Celtic mythology is a careful guess about a world we meet only through many hands.
